Requirement 1: LensKit must be used for all experiment functionality (data loading, preprocessing, model training, recommendation generation, and evaluation). No other frameworks should be called directly for core experiment operations.

Requirement 2: The three datasets must be loaded using LensKit's data loading functions: load_movielens() for MovieLens 100K, load_amazon_ratings() for Amazon Video Games (2014), and a suitable import for the HetRec Last.FM dataset (which may need to be loaded from a CSV file using DatasetBuilder or from_interactions_df).

Requirement 3: All datasets must be preprocessed with 5-core filtering (keeping only users and items with at least 5 interactions). For MovieLens 100K and Amazon Video Games (explicit feedback datasets), ratings > 3 must be converted to implicit feedback using binarize_ratings() with min_pos_rating=3.5. HetRec Last.FM (already implicit) must NOT be binarized.

Requirement 4: Data splitting must use a user-based holdout approach where for each user, 80% of interactions go to training and 20% to testing. LensKit's crossfold_users() with n_folds=1 and SampleFrac(0.2), or sample_users() with appropriate parameters and SampleFrac(0.2), should be used to achieve this 80/20 split.

Requirement 5: Exactly 5 different random seeds must be used for data splitting reproducibility. Each seed should produce a different 80/20 split. The rng parameter of the splitting function must be set to each seed value.

Requirement 6: Three LensKit algorithms must be used: ImplicitMFScorer (ALS for implicit feedback), ItemKNNScorer (Item-based k-NN), and PopScorer (Popularity baseline). All algorithms must use standard default hyperparameters.

Requirement 7: The experiment must run all combinations: 3 algorithms × 3 datasets × 5 seeds = 45 total runs. For each combination, train the model on the training split, generate top-N recommendations, and evaluate.
Requirement 8: Evaluation must use NDCG and Precision ranking metrics at cutoff values n=[1, 5, 10]. Use LensKit's MeasurementCollector with NDCG(n) and Precision(n) metrics.

Requirement 9: For each (algorithm, dataset, seed) combination, collect nDCG@k and Precision@k scores at k=1, 5, 10. Results must be aggregated across the 5 seeds, reporting mean and standard deviation per (algorithm, dataset, metric, k) combination, along with a short statistical analysis of the impact of random seed on accuracy.
